gears.name: a1
gears.source: [S2] Freeth 2021 SI Table S8; [S5] Freeth 2006 SI Notes 3 table; [S12] Voulgaris 2022
gears.arbor: axis a: input shaft perpendicular to all other arbors (crank). Voulgaris 2022 puts it on the right side of the case
gears.layer: front side of Main Plate, at the rim of b1 (contrate/crown gear)
gears.diameter_mm: avg outer radius 13.6+/-0.2, so outer diameter about 27.2 [S5]. Contrate gear, so Table S8 gives no module
gears.alternatives: Freeth 2006 CT: 48 'Definite'. Wright: 48 (limits 44-52). An earlier count of 45(48) is in the Price/Karakalos columns; which column is ambiguous in the extracted table [S5]
gears.notes: Fragment A. b1/a1 = 223/48, about 4.65 crank turns per year. It has a square/rectangular arbor with a large pin [S12]. In Freeth's models its tooth count does not affect any astronomical ratio

gears.name: b1
gears.arbor: axis b (outer arbor on the central axis of the front dials)
gears.layer: front side of Main Plate. It slides on 5 spacers and is held down by 4 brackets riveted to the Main Plate [S2 5.5.2]. It has 4 spokes (A,B,C,D) and 4 short + 4 long pillars on the rim
gears.function: Main Drive Wheel: 1 rev = 1 tropical year (mean Sun). In Freeth 2021 it is also the epicyclic carrier for the mean Sun, Nodes, Mercury and Venus trains, and it carries the Strap (short pillars) and the Circular Plate (long pillars)
gears.diameter_mm: outer diameter 130.0 (outer r 65.0, inner r 63.8), pitch diameter 128.8, thickness 2.7, module 0.578 [S2]. Avg outer r 64.9+/-1.1 [S5]. Wikipedia gives 'about 13 cm' [S8]
gears.alternatives: Karakalos 223-226. Price 225. Wright 223 (216-231). Freeth 2006: 223 (limits 223/224) [S5]. Voulgaris et al. 2022: 225 (219-225 measured on the deformed gear) [S12]. Voulgaris et al. 2024: 228 or 229 after a 3% shrinkage correction [S13]
gears.notes: Spoke features [S2 Fig S12]: A has a flat 10.5x10.3 mm at 31.6 mm and a countersink at 41.4 mm. B has a hole at 27.0 mm. C has a hole at 25.6 mm and a raised flat 14.2x12.0 mm at 46.2 mm. D has a pierced block at 31.8 mm (hole diameter 1.4). Long pillars are 32.0 total (27.5 to the shoulder). Short pillars are 20.4 total (16.2 to the shoulder)

gears.name: b2
gears.arbor: axis b, rigidly fixed to b1 through the Main Plate
gears.layer: behind Main Plate (rear gearing)
gears.function: year input for the rear trains: drives c1 (Moon train) and l1 (calendar and eclipse trains)
gears.diameter_mm: outer diameter 31.4 (r 15.7), pitch diameter 30.6, thickness 2.3, module 0.479
gears.notes: Derived centre distances from Table S8 pitch radii: b2-c1 25.1 mm, b2-l1 23.9 mm

gears.name: b3
gears.arbor: axis b, inner arbor (Moon arbor running through the b tube to the front Moon pointer)
gears.layer: behind Main Plate
gears.function: takes the Moon output (sidereal motion plus lunar anomaly) from e1 to the front Moon pointer
gears.diameter_mm: outer diameter 18.4, pitch diameter 17.4, thickness 1.3, module 0.546
gears.notes: e1-b3 centre distance about 17.9 mm (derived). Price's gear B4 = this b3; Price's 'B3' (32) and 'B6' (24) belong to his rejected scheme [S5]

gears.name: o1
gears.arbor: axis o = Olympiad (4-year games) dial pointer, inside the Metonic dial
gears.layer: back (upper back dial)

gears.diameter_mm: outer diameter 25.6 (outer r 12.8, inner r 12.2), pitch diameter 25.0, thickness 1.1, module 0.417. Avg outer r 13.3+/-0.1 [S5]

gears.name: q1 (Freeth naming) = Moon-phase contrate 'z'
gears.source: [S5] ('q1: small contrate gear in the Moon Phase Mechanism in Fragment C'); [S2] Table S8 and 6.2.6; [S11]
gears.arbor: short radial arbor in the Moon-pointer cap, turning the half-black/half-white Moon sphere (6 mm diameter)
gears.layer: FRONT, on the Moon pointer (back of Fragment C)
gears.function: Moon-phase differential: driven by b0 on the Sun tube, it shows the synodic phase (235/19 rev/yr relative to the Sun)
gears.diameter_mm: avg outer r 5.3+/-0.2 [S5]. Carman & Di Cocco: outer diameter 11.2, inner diameter 7, width 5.2 mm; about half survives with 10 teeth; tooth pitch about 1.7 mm [S11]
gears.alternatives: An earlier count of 24 appears in the 2006 table (Price or Wright column, ambiguous). Freeth 2006: 20 'Definite'
gears.notes: It is found with its teeth pointing away from the cap centre. Wright 2006 and Freeth 2021 assume it was re-assembled reversed; Freeth & Jones 2012 and Carman & Di Cocco 2016 keep the found orientation with a 4-gear drive. NAMING CLASH: Wikipedia and the Shambaugh diagram use q1 for the Callippic gear (60)

gears.name: r1
gears.arbor: Fragment D, unplaced. Freeth 2021 puts it on its own arbor pivoting in the 'D-plate' soldered to the Strap, as the Venus epicyclic pin gear. Voulgaris 2022/2024 put it on the a-shaft (with a1) driving a Draconic train
gears.layer: Freeth 2021: front, between b1 and the Strap (Venus is the last layer before the Strap). Voulgaris: right side of the case
gears.function: Freeth 2021: Venus g5 (51~44+34~26~63) carrying a pin on a riveted disk, with a slotted follower on the central axis. Voulgaris: drives s1 of the Draconic gearing
gears.diameter_mm: outer diameter 33.8 (r 16.9, inner r 15.9), pitch diameter 32.8, thickness 1.6 [Table S8] or 1.5 [S2 S5], module 0.521. The disk is riveted to the gear: radius 21.5 [S2] or 21.4 [S7], thickness 1.0. D-plate width 25.3, thickness 1.0
gears.alternatives: Karakalos 63. A count of 64 was considered by Freeth & Jones 2012 and rejected (61 teeth survive in 343.1 deg, and the 16.9 deg gap means 3 gaps) [S7]. Voulgaris 2022: 63 (61 preserved + 2 missing)
gears.notes: The letters 'ME' (=45) are inscribed on the gear and the disk. Freeth 2021 gives 63 = 3x7x3 (Venus factor 3x7 times multiplier 3). Venus pin distance d = 20.01 mm, i = 27.8 mm [S2 Table S9]. Voulgaris Draconic alternatives: r1 63 ~ s1 22 (b1=225); r1 63 ~ s1 57 + s2 56 ~ t1 22 (b1=229); or 63 ~ 34 + 61 ~ 40 (b1=228); or t1 = 20 [S12][S13]

gears.name: m3
gears.arbor: axis m (fixed with m1 and m2)
gears.layer: behind Main Plate
gears.function: drives e3. Sets the apsidal rate 477/4237 and feeds the Saros train
gears.diameter_mm: not measured. Pitch diameter about 12.6 at e3's module 0.466 (computed); m3-e3 centre distance about 58.2 mm (computed)
gears.notes: Missing gear (Wikipedia: m3, n1-3, p1-2 and q1 did not survive). The value is forced by the Saros and apsidal ratios

gears.diameter_mm: pitch diameter about 26.2 at module 0.495 (computed); m2-n1 centre distance about 17.0 mm (computed)
gears.notes: The tooth count is only fixed by the ratio; the physical gear is lost

gears.name: n_olympiad (Freeth 2008 'n3'; Wikipedia/Shambaugh 'n2')

gears.diameter_mm: estimated pitch radius 11.9, so pitch diameter about 23.8. The measured n-o interaxial distance is 24.4 mm = 11.9 + 12.5 [S6]

gears.function: drives p1 for the 76-year Callippic dial
gears.diameter_mm: about 7.5 pitch at m 0.5 (computed)
gears.notes: Freeth 2021 calls the Callippic dial 'a highly plausible conjecture' with no physical evidence; the only support is the '76 years' inscription [S2 1.2]

gears.name: p1

gears.name: p2

conflicts: b1 teeth: 223 is adopted (Freeth 2006, limits 223/224). Other counts: Karakalos 223-226, Price 225, Wright 223 (216-231) [S5]; Voulgaris 2022: 225, measured 219-225 [S12]; Voulgaris 2024: 228/229 after shrinkage correction [S13]. It affects no ratio in the Freeth models.
e3: 223 is adopted from the Saros cycle, but the CT best fit is 220-225 (limits 217-235). Karakalos and Price give 222 [S5].
e4: 188 is adopted (=4x47). CT gives 187-191; Price/Karakalos 192; Wright 191 [S5].
Lunar anomaly unit: 50/50/50/50 is adopted. CT gives e5 52 (50-52); Wright gives e5 51, e6 53, k1 49, k2 49; Price gives 32/48 [S5].
f1 53 vs 54 (Wright, Karakalos) vs 48 (Price). g1 54 vs 55 (Wright) vs 60 (Price). h1 60 vs CT 60-64. m1 96 vs 96/97. c2 48 vs CT 47/48 [S5].
r1: 63 vs 64 (considered and rejected by Freeth & Jones 2012). Missing teeth: 2 [S7][S12] vs 3 [S1][S2].
r1 role: Venus epicycle (Freeth & Jones 2012; Freeth 2021) vs Draconic train on the a-shaft (Voulgaris 2022/2024, extra gears s1 22 or s1 57+s2 56~t1 22 or 34+61~40) [S12][S13].
Naming n2/n3: Freeth 2008 SI calls the 57-tooth Olympiad driver n3 [S6]; Wikipedia/Shambaugh call it n2 and the 15-tooth Callippic driver n3 [S9]; Freeth 2006 called the 15-tooth gear n2 [S5].

Naming q1: Freeth 2006 SI and Freeth 2021 Table S8 use q1 for the surviving 20-tooth Moon-phase contrate (Fragment C). Wikipedia/Shambaugh use q1 for the hypothetical 60-tooth Callippic pointer gear. The data spec must rename one of them.
o1 was the Callippic pointer gear in 2006 (n2 15~p1 60+p2 12~o1 60) and was reassigned to the Olympiad dial in 2008 [S5][S6].
Mercury last gear: 20 (Fig 3e, main text, SI p.37) vs '40 ~ 24' in the SI Fig S22e caption. Only 20 gives 1513/480.

Freeth 2021 gear count: SI 6.3 says '29 of these gears include a1, b1 and everything behind b1', but listing Table S8 gives 28 behind b1 (27 in Fragment A + o1), with r1 and the contrate in front. 28+7=35 and 35+34=69 is consistent; with 29, the sums fail.
Mars uses multiplier x16 in Fig 3f, although SI 6.3 says a 'reasonable range is 7-10'.
Freeth & Jones 2012 superior-planet gear 3/4: the ISAW table gives Mars 70/70 and Jupiter 85/85; the Shambaugh diagram gives Mars 69/69 and Jupiter 86/86 [S7][S9].
Freeth & Jones 2012 totals: ISAW says 18 gears in front of b1 (12 superior + 6 inferior/solar) [S7]; Wikipedia says 30+7+17 = 54 gears plus 3 slotted bars [S8].

Moon phase: Wright 2006 and Freeth 2021 use a 2-gear differential with the contrate reversed (b0 20 ~ contrate 20). Freeth & Jones 2012 use 4 gears (Shambaugh: 27, 27, 20, 20). Carman & Di Cocco 2016 use 4 gears with a pin-and-slot on eccentric axes and keep the found orientation [S11].
Nodes: Freeth 2021 uses -5/93 (18.6 yr) and calls it explicitly hypothetical; the earlier suggestion was -12/223. Voulgaris proposes a Draconic pointer instead.

Calendar ring: Freeth 2021 SI 6.4.2 assumes 365 holes. Budiselic et al. 2020 find 354 [S15]. Woan & Bayley 2024 find 355.24 (+1.39/-1.36), or 354.08 (+1.47/-1.41) without holes near fractures, and call 365 'not plausible' [S14].
Mean module: 0.495 (Freeth 2021 Table S8) vs 0.47 (Freeth & Jones 2012). Wikipedia gives a mean circular pitch of 1.6 mm, thickness 1.4 mm and air gap 1.2 mm [S8].
Table S8 errors or inconsistencies: f1 outer radius 12.9 is smaller than inner radius 13.6 (swapped). r1 thickness is 1.6 (Table S8) vs 1.5 (SI S5). The r1 disk radius is 21.5 [S2] vs 21.4 [S7].
Lunar pin-and-slot: k offset about 1.1 mm, pin distance 9.6 mm (Freeth 2006) vs 9.9 mm (later). Both come only from search snippets [S19] and still need checking against the primary PDF.

Functionality: Szigety & Arenas 2025 find that with Edmunds' error model the triangular-tooth gears would jam or disengage, and question those error values [S16]. The Blender model needs clearance (Freeth & Jones 2012 add +0.2-0.4 mm to the sum of pitch radii).
Freeth 2021 CP modules are not published. The CP diameters here assume m = 0.5 and must be checked for clearance against the CP radius (b1 about 64 mm).

Not accessed directly: Price 1974 and Wright's papers (their counts come only from the Freeth 2006 SI comparison table), Jones 2017, Iversen 2017, Carman & Evans 2014, Wright 2002 planetary tooth counts, the Budiselic 2020 PDF (cited via Wikipedia). The Freeth 2021 SI Fig S20 back-gear diagram is a raster image and was not readable. No n4/n5 gear exists in any source found.

The other three are o1 in Fragment B, the 20-tooth Moon-phase contrate (Freeth's 'q1') in Fragment C, and r1 (63) in Fragment D. Wikipedia says 'at least 30'. FREETH 2021 FULL MODEL: 69 gears [S1][S2]. The 35 gears behind b1 are the 28 surviving ones plus 7 reconstructed: m3 27, n1 53, n 57, n 15, p1 60, p2 12, Callippic q1 60. The 34 gears in front of b1 are 2 surviving (r1 and the contrate), b0 20, 12 new gears between b1 and the Strap (fixed 51 and 49; Nodes 62, 64, 48; Venus 44, 34, 26; Mercury 72, 89, 40, 20) and 19 gears on the Circular Plate (fixed 56, shared 52 and 64, true-Sun 56, and 5 gears each for Saturn, Jupiter and Mars). That is 30 surviving + 8 reconstructed + 31 hypothetical = 69. The inventory above has 69 entries in exactly this split. Shared gears are counted once. FREETH & JONES 2012: 54 total per Wikipedia (30+7+17 plus 3 bars), but ISAW says 18 gears in front of b1. trains.pin_and_slot: LUNAR e-ASSEMBLY (SURVIVING, Freeth 2006 SI): axis e carries (1) turntable e3 (223 teeth, driven by m3 27) with e4 (188) riveted to it, turning at -477/4237 rev/yr (period 8.8826 yr); (2) an outer pipe turning freely inside e3 that carries e2 (32, driven by d2 127) and e5 (50), turning at -254/19; (3) an inner shaft carrying e6 (50) and e1 (32); e1 drives b3 (32) on the central Moon arbor. Mounted on e3: k1 (50) on axis K meshing with e5, and k2 (50) on axis K' meshing with e6. K' is offset from K by about 1.1 mm. A pin on the face of k1, about 9.6 mm from K, engages a radial slot in k2 (Freeth 2006, quoted via search result; the arXiv 2504.00327 paper cites +/-6.53 deg). WHY THE MEAN STAYS 254/19: in the frame of e3, (k1|e3) = -(50/50)(e5-e3). The pin and slot gives k2 exactly one turn per k1 turn (mean 1:1). Then (e6|e3) = -(50/50)(k2|e3). So the mean of (e6-e3) equals (e5-e3), which means e6 = e5 = -254/19 on average whatever e3 does. e1 -> b3 (32:32) flips the sign, so the Moon pointer runs at +254/19. WHY THE ANOMALY HAS THE ANOMALISTIC PERIOD: the angle between the pin and the fixed K->K' line (fixed on e3) advances at (k1|e3) = 254/19 - 477/4237 = 56165/4237 = (235/19)(239/223) per yr. That is the anomalistic month from 223 synodic = 239 anomalistic, 27.553 d. The apogee line (K->K') rotates with e3 at the apsidal rate. PIN-SLOT LAW for the Blender driver: let phi = k1 angle relative to e3, measured from the K->K' direction, r = pin radius, e = axis offset. Then k2 angle theta = atan2(r*sin(phi), r*cos(phi) - e), with the sign of e set by the direction of the offset. The output deviation is theta - phi. Its maximum is arcsin(e/r) = arcsin(1.1/9.6) = 6.58 deg (arctan form 6.54 deg; Freeth 2006 quotes 6.5 deg). It is periodic with zero mean. Then e6 = e3 - (k2|e3), and Moon = -e6. Freeth 2006 SI proves by vectors and by a mirror construction that this equals Hipparchos' epicyclic/eccentric lunar theory. The modules of e5/k1 and k2/e6 are adjusted slightly so e6 lies exactly on axis e (Freeth 2021 SI 4.2.1). PLANETS (HYPOTHETICAL, Freeth 2021): superior planets use the same indirect principle on the Circular Plate. The pin gear g5 turns at sigma/Y relative to the CP. Slot gear g6 sits on an eccentric axis at offset o = d/p (p = distance in AU). Equal output gear g7 on the central axis reverses the sense, so the output = CP(+1) - sigma/Y plus the epicyclic anomaly. Table S9 values: Mars o 6.58 / d 10.00 mm; Jupiter 1.58 / 8.22; Saturn 1.50 / 14.37. Inferior planets and the true Sun use a pin on the epicyclic gear (or its disk) plus a slotted follower pivoting on the central axis, with d = p x i. Mercury: i 36.0, d 14.04 mm. Venus: i 27.8, d 20.01 mm. True Sun: pin distance not published (suggest e = 1/24 of the carrier radius).
open_questions: b1 tooth count differs by source (all outputs are unaffected, only crank ratio and b1 pitch radius/module): Karakalos 223-226, Price 225, Wright 216-231, Freeth 2006 223 ('223/224'), German Wikipedia 224, Voulgaris 2022 ~225. Pick one for the spec and record the choice.

Several 'accepted' tooth counts are chosen to make ratios exact rather than directly counted. From the Freeth 2006 SI CT ranges: e3 220-225, e4 187-191, e5 50-52, k1 48-51, k2 48-52, e6 49/50, f1 53/54, g1 54-56, h1 60-64, m1 96/97, c1 38/39, c2 47-49. The model uses 223, 188, 50, 50, 50, 50, 53, 54, 60, 96, 38, 48.
Hypothetical back gears (m3 27, n1 53, n2 15, n3 57, p1 60, p2 12, Callippic q1 60) are inferred from dial functions. Treat them as RECONSTRUCTED, not SURVIVING.

Gear-name collisions between sources: 2006 'q1' = Moon-phase contrate (Freeth 2021 SI also says 'a1 and q1 are contrate gears') vs 2008/Wikipedia 'q1' = Callippic output; 2006 'o1' = Callippic output vs 2008 'o1' = Olympiad; English Wikipedia pairs Olympiad with n2 and Callippic with n3, but the Freeth 2008 primary source uses n3 (57) -> o1 (60). Use unique IDs in the data spec.

Freeth 2021 SI typos: Fig S22e caption says Mercury '40 ~ 24' (Fig 3e and main text say 40 ~ 20; only 20 gives 1513/480). The S4 formulas write (g1 x g3)/(g2 x g4) where g5 is meant (idlers do not change the ratio). The published Author Correction (Sci Rep 2021, PMC8385020) fixes only Greek characters and fraction formatting.

Freeth 2021 Supplementary Table S8 (measured module/pitch radius of every surviving gear, mean module 0.495) and Figs S20/S21/S23 (layer order, idler positions) are images in the SI PDF and were not transcribed here. They are needed for exact 3D centre distances. Known values: modules ~0.5; nodes 0.482/0.478; Venus 51 ~0.53, 44 ~0.54, 63/26/34 0.521; Mercury 72 at 31.6 mm; Nodes 62+64 arbor at 27.0 mm; b1 tip radius 65.0 mm; b1-Strap gap 15.0 mm (9 layers), Strap-CP 9.7 mm (5 layers); long pillars 32.0 mm, short 20.4 mm.

The lunar pin-and-slot geometry (offset ~1.1 mm, pin radius ~9.6 mm, ~6.5 deg) comes from the Freeth 2006 Nature main text. That text is paywalled and was seen only via search-engine quotation plus the '+/-6.53 deg (Freeth et al., 2006)' citation in arXiv 2504.00327. Verify against the article before fixing the CAD geometry.
True Sun: Freeth 2021 gives no pin eccentricity. Evans, Carman & Thorndike (2010) argue the solar anomaly was shown by an unevenly divided zodiac scale, not by gearing. Choose and flag it.

Moon phase: which input (mean Sun in Freeth 2021, or true Sun), the orientation of the surviving contrate gear (Wright's 2-gear solution needs it reversed), and the Carman & Di Cocco 2016 pin-and-slot phase variant remain open.

Nodes/draconic output is purely hypothetical. Candidates are Freeth 2021 -5/93 (exact, 4 gears on b1 Spoke B), Freeth & Jones 2012 -12/223, and Voulgaris 2022 b1-a1-r1(63)-s1(22), which is approximate and uses the Fragment D gear that Freeth 2021 assigns to Venus. Only one use of r1 can be modelled.

Jupiter's period relation (315,344) is not uniquely forced by Freeth 2021's criteria. Mercury (1513,480) and Mars (133,284) are argued to be unique; Venus (289,462) and Saturn (427,442) are backed by the numbers 462/442 in the Front Cover Inscription.

Sign/direction convention must be fixed once. Freeth uses positive = clockwise seen from the front. Back dials: Metonic, Callippic, Saros and Exeligmos run clockwise seen from the back (negative); the Olympiad dial is the only anticlockwise one (+1/4).

Calendar ring (not gear-driven): Woan & Bayley 2024 estimate 354.08 (+1.47/-1.41) holes without holes near fractures, or 355.24 (+1.39/-1.36) with all data. 360 is strongly disfavoured and 365 implausible. This affects the front-dial model.

A 2025 study (cited on English Wikipedia) argues that manufacturing errors in the original gears were too large for the mechanism to work well. arXiv 2504.00327 finds triangular teeth alone add negligible error. The Blender model should use ideal involute or triangular teeth and exact ratios, noting that this is idealized.

Sources not directly consulted in this pass: Price 1974, Jones 2017 'A Portable Cosmos', Budiselic et al. 2020 (only via Woan & Bayley), Iversen 2017, Carman & Evans 2014, Wright's 2005 gear-count papers. Their numbers are only quoted second-hand above (e.g. Karakalos/Price/Wright counts from the Freeth 2006 SI table).

open_questions: No published absolute (x,y) coordinates for the axes: the rear layout above is DERIVED (from Freeth 2006 radii + Price/Allen distances) and has mirror ambiguities (E, L, F sides; Olympiad/Callippic/Exeligmos angles). It needs checking against Freeth 2006 Fig. 2, Price Fig. 29 or CT data before we fix the data spec.

Freeth 2021 Supplementary Table S8 (module and radius of each surviving gear) exists only as an image inside the SI PDF. I could not extract it without writing a file. The Freeth 2006 SI radii were used instead; I checked their mean module against S8 (0.496 vs 0.495).
Freeth 2021 gives no numeric radii for the Cosmos rings. The ring radii above are visual estimates from Fig. 7.

Calendar ring count: 365 (traditional; used by Freeth 2021 and Voulgaris), 354 (Budiselic 2020), 354–355 (Woan & Bayley 2024) or ~352 (Malin & Dickens 2024). The user must choose; 354 also implies different/hypothetical gearing if the ring is driven.

Distance between the two back dial centres (Metonic–Saros): Price 141.0, Allen et al. 2016 145.5, Voulgaris re-positioning hypothesis ~154 mm. The derived layout reproduces Price (b–g 78) or Allen (b–g ~81.9).

Exact spiral construction parameters (offset between the two centres, start radius, slot width) from Anastasiou et al. 2014 were not accessible. Price's radii and Allen 2016's 73 mm / 6.7 mm are the only numbers found. A half-pitch offset of ~3.6 mm is implied but not verified.

Case depth is the least certain dimension: Price ~74 mm (1/4 Roman foot), Wikipedia 90 mm, AMRP ~100 mm. The front stack alone (b1 to CP front ≈ 6.4 + 29.5 mm plus sub-plate and dial plate) is ≥ 40–48 mm.
b1 tooth count 223 (Freeth) vs 224 vs 225 (Price, Voulgaris). e4 188 (adopted) vs 192 (Price/Karakalos).
Gear naming for the Olympiad/Callippic drives on axis n differs between sources (57 = n3 in Freeth 2008 SI; n2 in the Wikipedia schematic). The spec should use one convention.
Pin radius on k1 (lunar anomaly pin) and the slot length were not found in accessible sources. Only the ~1.1 mm axis eccentricity was found.
Input: a hand crank on a1 (Freeth, Price) versus Voulgaris et al.'s 'Lunar Disc' front input. The crank handle itself does not survive.

Physical functionality: Szigety & Arenas 2025 simulate jamming or disengagement with the measured manufacturing errors. Ideal geometry plus module adjustments (as Freeth 2021 did for Nodes and Venus) will be needed for a mechanically closing digital model. Triangular teeth need centre distance = sum of pitch radii + 0.1–0.4 mm.

Not read directly: Allen et al. 2016 (Almagest 7.1), Efstathiou et al. 2012 (MMT 52, axis distances), Wright's papers, Edmunds 2011, Jones 2017, Iversen 2017 and Carman & Evans 2014. Values attributed to Allen 2016 come via Voulgaris' citations.

A secondary GitHub project already builds Freeth 2021 in Blender 5.1 (Samizdat-Publications/antikythera). Its gear table has unsourced values (e.g. pin radius 9.67) and its axis directions come from Weibel's Sketchfab model. Use it only as a cross-check.

tooth_findings.finding: SURVIVING evidence: where teeth are well preserved, their shape is 'almost exactly that of an equilateral triangle' (60 deg). The exception is main drive wheel b1, whose teeth are larger and a little longer than wide, so the tooth angle is a little under 60 deg. Price says 'all gear teeth are exactly 60 deg equilateral triangles', in line with Heron and Vitruvius illustrations, and that such teeth work in de Dondi clock reconstructions.
tooth_findings.source: Price 1974, Gears from the Greeks, TAPS 64(7), pp. 25-26 and 51: https://gwern.net/doc/history/1974-desollaprice.pdf

tooth_findings.topic: A1b. Tooth shape as seen in CT
tooth_findings.finding: Freeth & Jones 2012 describe the teeth as 'triangular teeth with rounded tips and pits'. Thorndike 2020 shows that the profile conjugate to a triangle (the shape that gives uniform motion) is 'nearly triangular', a 'slightly rounded triangle'. Makers could therefore have smoothed the motion by rounding the triangles slightly.

The division of some gears is uneven. This suggests no dividing engine was used and the teeth were hand-cut with a file (Freeth & Jones 2012). Price: shaped by hand-sawing and filing. Wright: bronze stock 1-2 mm thick; filing fine teeth is easier in firm bronze. Efstathiou 2021: probably cold-forged thin bronze plates, sawn and hammer-levelled. On m2, a copper sheet 0.1-0.2 mm thick was fitted into the square central hole. It was probably a shim for an oversized or off-centre hole (Voulgaris 2022, from AMRP CT).
tooth_findings.source: ISAW Papers 4: http://dlib.nyu.edu/awdl/isaw/isaw-papers/4/ ; Price 1974 p.51 ; Efstathiou et al. 2021 Heritage 4:211 (https://digitalheritagelab.eu/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/heritage-04-00211-v4_compressed.pdf) ; Voulgaris et al. arXiv:2208.10997 section 5.2

tooth_findings.topic: A3. Tooth pitch and module (all values, sources disagree)
tooth_findings.finding: Price 1974: standard spacing 1.57 mm between teeth. b1 and a1 are coarser at about 1.75 mm. Fig. 32 fits 'diametral pitches' (= module) of 0.45 / 0.50 / 0.53 mm per tooth. Freeth & Jones 2012: mean module 0.47. Freeth et al. 2021 SI Table S8 (VGStudio CT measurements, pitch radius = (outer+inner)/2): mean module 0.495. My recomputation over 28 gears: range 0.417 (o1) to 0.578 (b1), SD 0.042. The 2021 main text designs hypothetical gears at a 'standard module' of 0.5. Wikipedia gives 'average circular pitch 1.6 mm' and cites ISAW 2012, but I could not find that number in the ISAW text. For reference: 0.47 gives a pitch of 1.48 mm, 0.495 gives 1.555 mm, 0.5 gives 1.571 mm. Module from outer radii in the Freeth 2006 SI (2R/(N+2), computed): 0.43-0.58.
tooth_findings.source: Price 1974 pp.26,29 ; ISAW Papers 4 section 1.7 ; Freeth 2021 SI MOESM4 Table S8: https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41598-021-84310-w/MediaObjects/41598_2021_84310_MOESM4_ESM.pdf ; Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antikythera_mechanism

tooth_findings.finding: Values disagree. (a) Outer minus inner best-fit radii in Freeth 2021 S8, which I computed over 28 gears: mean 0.82 mm, median 0.80, range 0.3 (m2) to 1.2 (b1). This is today's corroded state, with a stated error of up to ±0.5 mm on each radius. (b) Efstathiou et al. 2012 (MMT 52:219-231, paywalled), as quoted by Szigety & Arenas: average tooth height 1.1 mm. (c) Freeth & Jones 2012: 'length of the teeth is about 1.5 mm, depending on the module'. (d) Price: for equilateral teeth, radial length = sqrt(3)/2 x pitch, about 1.36 mm at 1.57 mm pitch (computed). A sharp equilateral tooth of pitch pi*m has height 2.72*m, i.e. 1.36 mm at m=0.5.
tooth_findings.source: Freeth 2021 SI Table S8 ; Szigety & Arenas 2025 footnote 3: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00327 ; ISAW Papers 4 section 4.2.3 ; Price 1974 p.25

tooth_findings.topic: A5. Gear thickness and layer spacing (3D data)
tooth_findings.finding: Freeth & Jones 2012: thickness 1.0-2.7 mm (b1 2.7, b2 2.3, m1 2.0, others 1.0-1.8, mean 1.3). Five layers e1-e6 are packed into about 7 mm, i.e. about 1.4 mm per gear. Their planet model uses 1.5 mm per layer (1.2 mm gear + 0.3 mm gap). Freeth 2021 S8 'Thick' column: e5 0.5, e6 0.6, k1 0.6, k2 0.5 mm (very thin); r1 1.6 mm. Freeth 2021: 15.0 mm free between b1 and the Strap, 9.7 mm between the Strap and the Circular Plate. The b1 tip radius of 65.0 mm and the 8.8 mm central tube limit epicyclic gears to under 100 teeth at m=0.5. Wikipedia's 'average wheel thickness 1.4 mm, air gap 1.2 mm' does not match the ISAW text it cites (1.3 mm mean thickness; 'little or no air gap').
tooth_findings.source: ISAW Papers 4 sections 1.7 and 3.6 ; Freeth 2021 SI sections 3.4 and 4.1.1 and Table S8 ; PMC full text: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7955085/

tooth_findings.topic: A6. Module mismatch between meshing gears (SURVIVING data)
tooth_findings.finding: Freeth 2021 SI: meshing gears have similar modules, with a mean mismatch of 3.7% and a maximum of 7.6% (b2 0.479 vs c1 0.517). Other pairs: b2-l1 5.3%, d2-e2 5.4%, e4-f1 5.4%, h2-i1 5.6%, b3-e1 4.8%. c1 and l1 both have 38 teeth but measured pitch radii of 9.8 vs 8.6 mm. Price noticed the same thing in 1974: c2(48)/d1(24) were cut with smaller teeth than usual, which he attributed to fitting two gear systems between one pair of axes (S8: c2 0.447, d1 0.452, the smallest). Freeth: e5-k1 and k2-e6 modules were adjusted by the maker so that e6 lands on axis e. Center distance approx (z1*m1 + z2*m2)/2 plus an allowance for loose triangular meshing.
tooth_findings.source: Freeth 2021 SI section 4.1.1 and 4.2.1 ; Price 1974 p.29

tooth_findings.topic: A7. Center-distance allowance used in reconstructions
tooth_findings.finding: Freeth & Jones 2012: 'inter-axial distance ... = sum of pitch radii + 0.2-0.3 mm' for the inferior-planet trains and '+0.4 mm' for the superior planets, 'since triangular-toothed gears cannot mesh too closely'. Freeth 2021 nodes train: modules 0.482 (49 and 62) and 0.478 (64 and 48), found by trial and error to allow loose fitting. The theoretical close-mesh values are 0.486 and 0.482 for a bearing at 27.0 mm.
tooth_findings.source: ISAW Papers 4 Figs. 42-43 notes ; Freeth 2021 SI section 4.2.1

tooth_findings.topic: A8. Tooth-count estimation method and uncertainty
tooth_findings.finding: Freeth 2006: maximum-likelihood fit of tooth-tip angles to a model theta_n = a + n*360/T, scanning T for peaks. Counts are sensitive to the assumed centre: for e3 (R 52.3 mm) and h1 (R 14 mm), a 1 mm centre shift changes the count over a semicircle by about 3. e3 centre is within 0.3 mm (max error 0.4 mm), h1 within 0.2 mm. Whole tooth sectors can be displaced several mm relative to the hub. Price: measuring the radius at tip or root instead of mid-tooth gives an error of ±2.7 teeth, so counts from radius may be 2-3 too high. Woan & Bayley 2024 (Bayesian, calendar ring): 355.24 (+1.39/-1.36) holes, or 354.08 (+1.47/-1.41) when holes near fractures are excluded. This is an analogous division-count method.
tooth_findings.source: Freeth 2006 SI Suppl. Notes 3: https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fnature05357/MediaObjects/41586_2006_BFnature05357_MOESM1_ESM.pdf ; Price 1974 p.25 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00040

tooth_findings.topic: A9. Disputed counts: surviving wheels whose count is partly inferred
tooth_findings.finding: b1: Karakalos 223-226, Price 225, Wright 216-231, Freeth 2006 223 (limits 223/224, 'reason for 223 or 224 not known'). Voulgaris et al. 2022 measured 219-225 on the shrunken wheel, argue the original lies near the upper limit, and use 225. The b1 radius varies ±1.1 mm and its two hubs are offset about 0.4 mm. e3: Freeth best-fit 220-225, limits 217-235; 223 is adopted from the Saros (RECONSTRUCTED). e4: best fit 187-191, limits 180-192; 188 is adopted (RECONSTRUCTED by function). e5: fit 52 (limits 50-52); e6 50 (49/50); k1 49/50; k2 50 (48-52). 50 is adopted for all four (RECONSTRUCTED). Definite counts: a1 48, b3 32, d1 24, d2 127, e1 32, e2 32, f2 30, g2 20, h2 15, l1 38, l2 53, m2 15, r1 63.
tooth_findings.source: Freeth 2006 SI table ; Voulgaris et al. 2022 MAA 22(3):103-131 (arXiv:2104.06181) section 3.6

tooth_findings.finding: Edmunds measured random tooth-placement error as a fraction of the angular pitch: 0.04-0.08. He also found a systematic sinusoidal or eccentricity error of 0-2 deg, with 0.5-1 deg seen on some gears. Model results: Case A (0 deg, 0.04) gives Metonic sigma 0.32 deg (1.2 d); Case D (2 deg, 0.08) gives lunar pointer 26-57 deg and Saros up to 8.6 deg (39 d). Edmunds concluded the lunar-anomaly output was largely swamped by gear errors and the device worked more as a display than for precise calculation.
tooth_findings.source: Edmunds 2011 JHA 42(3):307-320 (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252740767), numbers as tabulated in Szigety & Arenas 2025 Table 2: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00327

tooth_findings.finding: Triangular teeth are not conjugate, so the driven gear speeds up and slows down within each tooth passage. The ratio is exact only after whole numbers of teeth. The fastest/slowest speed ratio is about (r_max/r_min)^2: close to 1 for large gears, large for small pinions (two 10-tooth gears: 9/7 to 7/9). Contact switches between tip-on-flank phases, the next teeth must engage before d(theta) reaches 0, and gears jam if the pressure angle exceeds atan(1/mu). Closed form for the tip-on-flank phase: theta(phi) = asin(R sin phi / q) + asin(R sin alpha / q) - alpha, with q^2 = R^2 + Y^2 - 2RY cos phi.
tooth_findings.source: Thorndike 2020, 'Triangular gear teeth', in Instruments-Observations-Theories (CC BY), doi 10.5281/zenodo.3975713: https://archive.nyu.edu/bitstream/2451/61288/46/01.%20Thorndike.pdf

tooth_findings.topic: A12. Can triangular teeth work? (simulation of real trains)
tooth_findings.finding: Szigety & Arenas 2025: with perfect triangular teeth (h = 1.1 mm, radii from Freeth 2006), tooth shape alone gives negligible pointer error: lunar sigma 0.60 deg (Dm 1.84), Metonic 0.053 deg (0.20 d), Saros 0.038 deg. Clearance G (tip-to-valley, as % of h) must be about 40%: below 10% jams, above ~87-90% disengages. With Edmunds' measured errors, 90% of runs jammed (lunar train after ~129 d, Metonic after 234 d, Saros after 121 d). The largest tolerable errors are about 0.04 random and 0.1 deg eccentricity. Big wheels (d2-e2, m3-e3, e4-f1, l2-m1) are the most jam-prone because eccentricity scales with radius. The authors conclude the real errors were probably smaller than Edmunds' CT-based values, which corrosion and CT resolution would inflate. Physical tests: Voulgaris replaced involute 9/47 gears with triangular 18/94 on a telescope drive. Motion was intermittent, tooth-by-tooth error about 2x worse than involute, noise about 74 dB vs 53 dB, but it ran. AUTH built functional 1:1 (2011) and 3:1 (2017) replicas with triangular teeth; they take up gaps by turning until all pointers move and approaching a date from one direction.
tooth_findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00327 ; Voulgaris et al. arXiv:2208.10997 section 5.1 ; Efstathiou et al. 2021 Heritage 4:211 sections 3 and 4.6

tooth_findings.topic: A13. Computed: triangular-tooth transmission error for AM-size pairs
tooth_findings.finding: My in-memory numpy simulation: straight-flank triangular teeth, m=0.5, h=1.1 mm, a = rp1 + rp2 + G*h. At G=0.4h the peak-to-peak error on the driven wheel was: 15:60 0.38 deg (6.3% of its pitch); 15:53 0.42 deg; 20:60 0.28 deg; 24:48 0.28 deg; 32:32 0.27 deg; 38:64 0.13 deg; 50:50 0.12 deg; 53:188 0.03 deg. Instantaneous speed ratio relative to nominal: 0.59-1.23 for 15-tooth pinions, 0.93-1.08 for 50:50. Backlash at G=0.4h is about 0.66 mm of arc at the pitch circle, about 42% of the pitch. When rotated at exact constant ratio from a mid-backlash start, 15:60, 20:60, 32:32 and 38:64 had zero collisions over 4 driver pitches (minimum slack ≥ 1.1 deg; 0.47 deg at G=0.2h). So triangular teeth are safe for a Blender model animated by exact-ratio drivers, but they add large backlash that accumulates along a train.
tooth_findings.source: Computed this session (numpy, Blender-bundled Python 3.13); geometry per Szigety & Arenas 2025 and Efstathiou 2012 h=1.1 mm

tooth_findings.finding: Eccentricity e on a gear of radius R gives an angular error of about atan(e/R). m2 (R 4.2 mm, 15 teeth) with e = 0.2 mm gives 2.79 deg, which reaches the Metonic pointer as about 0.79 deg (one cell is about 7.66 deg). b1 (130 mm diameter) with e = 0.2 mm gives 0.176 deg, or about ±2.36 deg on the proposed Draconic pointer. For comparison, hand-made geared devices typically show 0.1-0.4 mm dimensional errors vs about 0.02-0.05 mm today. Lesson for the model: keep bores concentric; any intentional error must be a parameter.

tooth_findings.topic: A15. Do not build from mean measured radii
tooth_findings.finding: AUTH's first replica (about 2008-2010) used the Freeth 2006 mean diameters, which carry a tolerance of about 1 mm. It did not work: some pairs jammed (too large for the axial distance) and others did not touch. The working 2011 models came from FORTRAN algorithms that used tooth counts plus a common 'root angle' to find a common module for all gears, then computed axial distances checked against CT distances measured by two PhD fellows.
tooth_findings.source: Efstathiou et al. 2021 Heritage 4:211 section 3 ; Efstathiou et al. 2012 MMT 52:219-231: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0094114X12000316

tooth_findings.topic: A16. Computed: involute options that keep original counts
tooth_findings.finding: Undercut-free minimum tooth count with ha*=1: 17.1 at alpha=20 deg (z=15 needs x ≥ +0.12, z=12 needs x ≥ +0.30), 11.2 at 25 deg, 8.0 at 30 deg. Tip land at m=0.5: z=15 gives 0.33 / 0.24 / 0.13 mm at 20 / 25 / 30 deg; z=223 gives 0.41 / 0.31 / 0.20 mm. Contact ratio for AM pairs at 20 / 25 / 30 deg: 15:60 1.63 / 1.46 / 1.34; 32:32 1.67 / 1.48 / 1.36; 27:223 1.77 / 1.54 / 1.40; 50:50 1.75 / 1.54 / 1.39. Key point: a rack with equilateral-triangle teeth is exactly the basic rack of a 30 deg involute system with sharp tips (full height 2.72*m). A 30 deg involute therefore reproduces the ancient 60 deg flank geometry for large wheels while staying conjugate.
tooth_findings.source: Computed this session (standard involute formulas: z_min = 2*ha/sin^2(alpha); tip thickness via inv(alpha); contact ratio via line of action)

tooth_findings.topic: A17. Computed: imposed center distances need per-pair module and/or profile shift
tooth_findings.finding: Formulas: alpha_w = acos(a0*cos(alpha)/a_w), x1+x2 = (z1+z2)(inv alpha_w - inv alpha)/(2 tan alpha). Case 1, Freeth nodes train 49~62+64~48 (111 vs 112 teeth, coaxial, bearing at 27.0 mm). At m=0.486: x_sum +0.06 and -0.43 (alpha 20 deg; -0.44 at 30 deg). At m=0.5: x_sum -1.33 and -1.69, which is too large, so choose the module per pair as Freeth did. Case 2, pin-and-slot e5~k1 vs k2~e6 (all 50 teeth, k axes offset about 1.1 mm). S8 radius sums give 25.6 vs 26.9 mm, which means pair modules of about 0.512 and 0.538; one m=0.5 for both would need x_sum +1.3 and +4.7. Case 3, b2 in two meshes (c1 and l1, both 64:38). S8 radius sums (25.1 vs 23.9 mm) cannot both be met with one b2 module without x_sum spanning +0.23 to -1.78, so let the c and l arbors be placed by the layout solver. Equal-base-pitch alternative: b2 (m 0.479, 20 deg) would mesh with a 0.517-module c1 only at alpha 29.5 deg. Loop closures to solve: b-c-d-e (b2~c1, c2~d1, d2~e2) with b3~e1, and b-l-m-e (b2~l1, l2~m1) with m3~e3.
tooth_findings.source: Computed this session; inputs from Freeth 2021 SI Table S8 and section 4.2.1; 1.1 mm pin-and-slot offset from Efstathiou et al. 2021 Heritage 4:211

tooth_findings.finding: Freeth 2021 S8 row f1 lists outer radius 12.9 < inner radius 13.6, apparently transposed. The Freeth 2006 SI gives f1 inner 13.6 and outer 14.6 with a mean tip radius of 14.0, so the two sources conflict. Freeth 2006 f1: centre 'could be a few millimetres in any direction'. c1: centre 'almost impossible to identify accurately'. Treat S8 radii of c1, f1, l1 and h2 as soft data.
tooth_findings.source: Freeth 2021 SI Table S8 ; Freeth 2006 SI gear notes

teeth_models.profile_recommendation:
RECOMMENDATION FOR THE BLENDER DATA SPEC (keep every original tooth count; drive motion with exact rational ratios; tooth geometry only needs to be conjugate and collision-free).

1) MASTER PROFILE: involute generated from a 30 deg pressure-angle basic rack ('historical involute').
- Parameters: ha* = 1.0, hf* = 1.25, tip and root fillets of about 0.15-0.25 m, which gives the 'rounded tips and pits' that ISAW 2012 describes.
- Why 30 deg: a rack of equilateral-triangle teeth is exactly a 30 deg involute basic rack with sharp tips. The large wheels (b1, e3, e4, d2, m1) look like Price's 60 deg triangles, yet every mesh keeps a constant velocity ratio.
- Depth: whole depth 2.25 m = 1.125 mm at m = 0.5, which matches measured tooth heights (S8 outer minus inner, mean 0.82 mm, range 0.3-1.2; Efstathiou 2012 average 1.1 mm).
- No undercut anywhere, because z_min is 8 and the smallest AM wheels have 12-15 teeth.
- Contact ratio is 1.32-1.42 on AM pairs (computed), which is enough.
- Tip land is 0.13 mm at z = 15 and 0.20 mm at z = 223 (m = 0.5).
- Backlash: thin the teeth rather than move the axes, so arbor positions stay where the layout solver puts them. Suggested circumferential backlash for a render-only model: about 0.02-0.05 mm (engineering rule of thumb, not sourced).

2) OPTIONAL PRESETS in the same generator.
- 'Modern' alpha = 20 deg (ISO 53 rack): contact ratio 1.6-1.8. Needs profile shift x ≥ +0.12 at z = 15 and x ≥ +0.30 at z = 12. Best if the model is later 3D-printed at an enlarged scale.
- 'Ancient' straight-flank 60 deg triangles, for rendering only:
  - Center distance a = rp1 + rp2 + G*h with G ≈ 0.4h. This is the Szigety & Arenas optimum: below 10% jams, above ~87-90% disengages. Freeth & Jones 2012 used +0.2-0.3 mm and +0.4 mm.
  - My simulation at G = 0.4h: 0.03-0.42 deg peak-to-peak error on the driven wheel, speed ratio 0.59-1.23x nominal for 15-tooth pinions, backlash about 42% of the pitch.
  - Rotated at exact ratio from a mid-backlash start, it never collided.
  - Not suitable as the 'functional' master: it is not conjugate, backlash accumulates over 5-7 meshes, and it is sensitive to errors.
- Cycloidal: not recommended. It needs an exact center distance, has no profile-shift practice, needs a generating circle per pair, and the ratio stops being constant once the center distance is off.

3) MODULES AND DIAMETERS.
- For a conjugate pair the operating pitch radii are fixed by the center distance: r'_i = a*z_i/(z1+z2). 'Near-original diameters' therefore comes down to choosing a.
- Surviving gears: start from Freeth 2021 S8 modules (0.417-0.578, mean 0.495). Hypothetical gears: m = 0.5, as Freeth 2021 does.
- Both gears in a mesh must share the same base pitch; in practice use the same m and the same alpha.
- Set one module per mesh: m_w = 2a/(z1+z2). Measured partners differ by 3.7% on average (7.6% max), so a shared module moves each measured radius by at most ~5% (≤0.45 mm). That is inside Freeth 2006's ±0.5 mm radius uncertainty.
- Never copy measured mean radii directly. AUTH's first replica did, and it jammed or lost contact.

4) CENTER DISTANCES.
- Free meshes: a = m_w(z1+z2)/2 exactly. A layout solver closes the loops b-c-d-e (with b3~e1) and b-l-m-e (with m3~e3) and respects the CT and inscription positions.
- Hard constraints:
  - coaxial epicyclic trains (Freeth nodes 49~62+64~48, bearing at 27.0 mm)
  - pin-and-slot e5~k1 vs k2~e6 (k axes offset about 1.1 mm, so different distances for two 50:50 meshes)
  - a gear shared by several meshes (b2 with c1 and l1; fixed 51 for Mercury and Venus; fixed 56 for the superior planets)
  - spoke bearings at 27.0, 25.6 and 31.6 mm
- For hard constraints, first choose a per-pair module (Freeth used 0.482 and 0.478), then trim with profile shift:
  - alpha_w = acos(a0*cos(alpha)/a_w)
  - x1+x2 = (z1+z2)(inv alpha_w - inv alpha)/(2 tan alpha)
  - Keep |x_sum| ≲ 1 and each |x| ≲ 0.6 (rule of thumb).
  - Worked example: nodes at m = 0.486 need x_sum +0.06 and -0.43, whereas a single m = 0.5 would need -1.33 and -1.69.

5) VERIFICATION IN BLENDER.
- Store ratios as Fractions in the spec and drive rotations with exact-ratio drivers.
- For every mesh, sweep at least one full relative cycle (lcm of the tooth counts, in teeth) and test interference with mathutils.bvhtree.BVHTree.overlap, or with a 2D numpy polar-profile test like the one used here. Assert backlash > 0, contact ratio ≥ 1.2, no undercut, and tip land > 0.
- Do not rely on Bullet rigid-body physics at 0.5 mm module.
- Take gear thicknesses from S8 or ISAW (0.5-2.7 mm) and the layer pitch as about 1.4-1.5 mm.

recommendations.topic: 0. Overall architecture: one data spec with a pure-Python core, and Blender used only for building and rendering
recommendations.recommendation: Use one versioned data spec (TOML, read with the stdlib tomllib in Blender's bundled Python 3.13, validated with the bundled fastjsonschema) as the only source of truth. A pure-Python package with no bpy or mathutils imports computes three things: (a) exact kinematics with fractions.Fraction, (b) 2D gear outlines with numpy, (c) the Blender driver-expression strings. Blender scripts only turn these arrays and strings into objects, drivers, materials and exports. This way the geometry and motion that are verified are exactly the ones rendered and printed. Give every gear, arbor or joint record the fields status (SURVIVING / RECONSTRUCTED / HYPOTHETICAL), sources [URLs] and alternatives [{value, source}], so disagreements between sources stay visible. Copy these fields into each Blender object's custom properties and use them for viewport colour-coding.
recommendations.api_details: Measured in memory on this Mac (Blender 5.2.2, M4): the bundled python3.13 has numpy 2.3.4, tomllib, fastjsonschema 2.21.1, tomli_w 1.2.0 and unittest. It has no pytest, scipy or shapely. /usr/bin/python3 is 3.9.6 and has no tomllib, so use /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/Resources/5.2/python/bin/python3.13 for everything outside Blender. Freeth 2021 counts 69 gears in total (34 in front of b1 and 35 behind), so budget for about 70 gear bodies.

recommendations.topic: 1a. Involute tooth profile in numpy: the maths
recommendations.recommendation: Generate each gear as closed 2D loops: one outer tooth loop plus hole loops for the bore, the square arbor hole and the spoke windows. Use the ISO 53 profile A rack by default: alpha=20 deg, ha*=1.0, hf*=1.25, rho_f*=0.38. Per gear: r=m*z/2, rb=r*cos(alpha), ra=r+m*(1+x), rf=r-m*(1.25-x). The flank half-angle at radius rho is psi(rho) = (pi/2 + 2*x*tan(alpha))/z + inv(alpha) - inv(alpha_rho), where alpha_rho=arccos(rb/rho) and inv(a)=tan(a)-a. The flank points for tooth k are rho*(cos(k*2pi/z +/- psi), sin(...)), with rho running from max(rb, r_form) to ra. Add a short tip arc and a root arc or fillet. For backlash, thin each tooth by j_t/2: psi -= j_t/(4r). Under the base circle, either use the exact trochoid (1b) or a radial line plus a circular fillet of radius 0.38m.
recommendations.api_details: Measured with a vectorised numpy prototype: a 223-tooth outline (24 flank points per side, 4 tip and 4 root points) has 12,488 points and takes 3.3 ms. The same code validated the backlash maths inside Blender: with 0.05 mm of thinning per gear and the gear centred in the gap, the measured flank clearance was 0.04703 mm, against the theoretical 0.05*cos20 deg = 0.04698 mm. Contact ratio: eps = (sqrt(ra1^2-rb1^2) + sqrt(ra2^2-rb2^2) - a*sin(alpha_w)) / (pi*m*cos(alpha)). Computed values: 64/38 gives 1.749, 223/15 gives 1.70, 15/15 gives 1.48. The formula overestimates when a gear is undercut.

recommendations.topic: 1b. Undercut, profile shift and root fillet
recommendations.recommendation: The mechanism has small pinions, some with 15 teeth. At 20 deg, any gear with z < 17.1 is undercut. For those, use a profile shift x >= 1 - z*sin^2(alpha)/2 (z=15 gives x>=0.123, z=16 gives x>=0.064), or switch to 25 deg (z_min=11.2). A profile shift changes the working centre distance: inv(alpha_w) = 2*tan(alpha)*(x1+x2)/(z1+z2) + inv(alpha), then a = m*(z1+z2)/2 * cos(alpha)/cos(alpha_w). Choose x1 = -x2 wherever the measured centre distance must stay unchanged. For the root, compute the true generated fillet: the trochoid traced by the rack tip-radius centre, offset by rho_f. Unit-test it against a brute-force numeric envelope of the rack sampled at many roll angles, using pure numpy.
recommendations.api_details: Values computed in memory: z_min(20 deg)=17.097 and z_min(25 deg)=11.198. Build a verify.py rule that fails any mesh without an explicit x, or with alpha too small for its z.

recommendations.topic: 1c. Historical triangular teeth (optional mode)
recommendations.recommendation: Offer a per-gear tooth_form of 'involute' (the default, used for the physically functional model) or 'triangular', which matches the originals. Wikipedia reports equilateral teeth with an average circular pitch of 1.6 mm, wheels about 1.4 mm thick and a mean air gap of about 1.2 mm. Triangular teeth are not conjugate, so the instantaneous ratio fluctuates within each tooth pitch (Thorndike's analysis, used by Szigety & Arenas 2025). Constant-ratio drivers will therefore show small gaps or penetration. In triangular mode, either give generous backlash, or run a 2D contact solver in pure Python: for each driver angle, root-find the driven angle at which the profiles touch. Then store the result as a lookup table (see 2e). The mean ratio over a full turn stays exactly z1/z2.
recommendations.api_details: The Szigety & Arenas 2025 simulation concludes that the triangular shape alone causes negligible error, but that the manufacturing errors estimated by Edmunds (2011) would cause jamming or disengagement.

recommendations.topic: 1d. Module assignment, centre distances and mesh phasing
recommendations.recommendation: Real modules vary from about 0.44 to 0.58 (Shambaugh's CAD used a uniform 0.5 and reports a resulting collision). So assign the module per connected component of the tooth-mesh graph: a gear whose single set of teeth meshes two partners forces all three to share one module. Solve the arbor XY positions by least squares, fixing the CT-measured main axes and applying the exact constraints a_ij = m*(z_i+z_j)/2 (profile-shift corrected where used). Report the residuals against the measured positions. Assembly phase: with tooth 0 of each gear at local angle 0 and line of centres beta from i to j, set phi_j0 = beta + pi + pi/z_j - (z_i/z_j)*(phi_i0 - beta) for external meshes. Propagate phases through the gear tree; for any closed loop, check the phase is consistent.
recommendations.api_details: This phasing formula was checked in Blender with a 64/38 pair: 25 samples over one tooth pitch gave 0 BVH overlaps each, while a phase shifted by half a pitch gave 678 to 718 overlapping triangle pairs.

recommendations.topic: 1e. Building meshes in bpy (fast, exact, headless)
recommendations.recommendation: Triangulate the caps inside Blender with mathutils.geometry.tessellate_polygon([outer, bore, window1..n]), passing 3D tuples; it supports holes. Build the prism from numpy arrays: bottom triangles reversed, top triangles offset by n, and side quads per loop. Write them with foreach_set and do not use from_pydata or per-tooth bmesh operations. Use smooth shading plus set_sharp_from_angle; auto-smooth was removed in 4.1. Avoid Boolean modifiers on verified geometry. If one is unavoidable, use solver 'MANIFOLD' (4.5+), which needs manifold inputs.
recommendations.api_details: me=bpy.data.meshes.new(n); me.vertices.add(N); me.vertices.foreach_set('co', V.astype(float32).ravel()); me.loops.add(L); me.loops.foreach_set('vertex_index', idx); me.polygons.add(P); me.polygons.foreach_set('loop_start', starts); me.update(calc_edges=True); me.validate(); me.shade_smooth(); me.set_sharp_from_angle(angle=radians(30)). Measured on this M4: a 223-tooth gear (25,072 vertices, 37,608 faces) builds in 19.9 ms, and validate() changed nothing. 70 gears (579k vertices) build in 0.53 s in total. The signed-volume check on the closed mesh was positive (19,349 mm^3, about the expected 19,372 mm^3). For a bore plus 4 spoke windows, the tessellation area matched the analytic value within polygonisation error. Boolean solver enum in 5.2.2: FLOAT, EXACT, MANIFOLD.

recommendations.topic: 1f. Geometry Nodes vs numpy, and the Extra Objects gear primitive
recommendations.recommendation: Use numpy plus direct mesh construction as the primary method. With Geometry Nodes, the verified geometry would live in a node graph that pure-Python tests cannot evaluate, and the modifier API changed again in 5.2. Keep Geometry Nodes for optional decoration only, such as dial ticks, spiral cells and inscriptions via instancing. Do not use 'Add Mesh: Extra Objects' mesh.primitive_gear. It is not bundled since 4.2 (it is now the extension add_mesh_extra_objects v0.4.1, 4.2+), and its tooth is a 4-point trapezoid approximation, not an involute.
recommendations.api_details: 5.2 GN modifier inputs: md.properties.inputs.<Socket_id>.value = v (also .type='ATTRIBUTE' and .attribute_name). Verified on 5.2.2: the old md['Socket_0']=v now raises TypeError 'id properties not supported for this type'. Sockets: ng.interface.new_socket(name, in_out='INPUT', socket_type='NodeSocketInt'). Relevant node idnames present in 5.2.2: GeometryNodeRepeatInput/Output, GeometryNodeForeachGeometryElementInput/Output, GeometryNodeFillCurve, GeometryNodeExtrudeMesh, GeometryNodeCurveStar, GeometryNodeMeshBoolean, GeometryNodeInstanceOnPoints, GeometryNodeRealizeInstances. In factory startup, bpy.ops.mesh has no gear operator.

recommendations.topic: 1g. Units and scale
recommendations.recommendation: Model with 1 Blender unit = 1 mm: scene.unit_settings.system='METRIC', length_unit='MILLIMETERS', scale_length=0.001. Do not model in metres. Tooth features are about 0.5 to 0.8 mm, so tools with default thresholds of 0.0001 m (Merge by Distance) and the 0.04 rigid-body margin would damage or swamp the geometry at metre scale. Vertex coordinates are float32; at 70 mm the precision step is about 8e-6 mm, which is fine.
recommendations.api_details: UnitSettings properties in 5.2.2: system, system_rotation, scale_length, use_separate, length_unit, mass_unit, time_unit, temperature_unit.

recommendations.topic: 2a. Kinematic solver (pure Python, exact)
recommendations.recommendation: Represent the mechanism as rigid bodies (arbor assemblies) placed in parent frames (world, or a carrier body such as the e3 turntable) and linked by typed joints: fixed (same arbor), external_mesh, internal_mesh, crown/contrate, pin_slot, spiral_follower. Solve every angle relative to the parent frame (Willis): omega_p - omega_c = -(z_s/z_p)*(omega_s - omega_c) for a planet on carrier c meshing gear s. Store the linear parts as a Fraction ratio times crank plus a phase, and the non-linear parts as explicit terms. verify.py then checks every astronomical cycle as an exact rational identity: an output completes N turns in exactly M crank turns. Keep the targets and their sources in the spec. Emit (1) a closed-form driver expression per body and (2) expected world matrices for any crank value, used by the in-Blender checks.
recommendations.api_details: Freeth 2021: Mercury and Venus use 5-gear mechanisms with pin-and-slotted followers, and Mars, Jupiter and Saturn use 7-gear indirect mechanisms with pin-and-slot devices. The pin_slot joint must therefore be generic: the pin may ride on an epicyclic gear and the follower can be a slotted lever.

recommendations.topic: 2b. Master crank and drivers (recommended over baked keys)
recommendations.recommendation: Create one Empty 'AM_Controller' with an ID property 'crank' measured in turns of b1, i.e. years. Every rotating body gets a driver on rotation_euler[2] with one SINGLE_PROP variable reading ctl['crank']. Write every expression in Blender's Simple Expression subset. Simple expressions run without Python and without the Auto-Run trust prompt, are fast (about 0.16 ms per frame measured with 150 drivers) and behave identically in the UI and in -b mode. For interactive use, turn the crank value or mute its F-curve and drag it. For playback, keyframe crank linearly with LINEAR extrapolation. The pure-Python verifier evaluates the same expression strings in a restricted namespace containing only Blender's simple-expression functions, and a linter rejects any other name.
recommendations.api_details: fc=obj.driver_add('rotation_euler',2); d=fc.driver; d.type='SCRIPTED'; v=d.variables.new(); v.name='c'; v.type='SINGLE_PROP'; v.targets[0].id_type='OBJECT'; v.targets[0].id=ctl; v.targets[0].data_path='["crank"]'; d.expression='fmod(c*254/19+0.123,1)*2*pi'; then assert d.is_simple_expression and d.is_valid and d.expression==expr. Allowed: frame, pi, True/False, + - * / == != < <= > >= and/or/not, the ternary, min max radians degrees abs fabs floor ceil trunc round int sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 exp log sqrt pow fmod lerp clamp smoothstep. Controller: ctl['crank']=0.0; ctl.id_properties_ui('crank').update(min=..., description=...). Animate: ctl.keyframe_insert('["crank"]', frame=f); cb=bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_get_channelbag_for_slot(ctl.animation_data.action, ctl.animation_data.action_slot); set each fcurve's extrapolation='LINEAR' and each key's interpolation='LINEAR'. All of this was verified on 5.2.2.

recommendations.topic: 2c. Driver limits and precision (verified pitfalls)
recommendations.recommendation: (1) Blender silently truncates driver expressions to 255 characters: a 599-character string was stored as 255. Keep expressions short: write exact ratios as integer fractions (c*254/19), and for long non-linear chains store intermediate unwrapped angles in driven custom properties on joint Empties. Always assert that the stored expression equals the one generated. (2) Driver inputs and outputs are float32. At crank=12345.678 the driver result matched float32(c) and was 0.0027 rad away from the float64 value. Keep |crank| within about 100 turns (under 0.05 deg of error), or pass the crank as an integer turn plus a fraction. Wrap with fmod(...,1)*2*pi inside the expression, but never feed a wrapped angle into a later ratio. (3) Read rotations with SINGLE_PROP 'rotation_euler[2]', or TRANSFORMS with transform_space='TRANSFORM_SPACE'. In a 5.2.2 test, TRANSFORMS with LOCAL_SPACE did not return the raw multi-turn angle (10 rad came back as 4*pi), while TRANSFORM_SPACE and SINGLE_PROP returned 10.0. (4) Setting an ID property from Python does not re-evaluate the depsgraph by itself: call ctl.update_tag() and view_layer.update(), or use scene.frame_set().
recommendations.api_details: Driver.bl_rna.properties['expression'].length_max == 256; DriverVariable name is limited to 64 characters. DriverVariable.type values: SINGLE_PROP, TRANSFORMS, ROTATION_DIFF, LOC_DIFF, CONTEXT_PROP.
recommendations.source: local in-memory tests on Blender 5.2.2 LTS

recommendations.topic: 2d. Epicyclic trains via parenting and the pin-and-slot as a simple expression
recommendations.recommendation: Make each carrier (e.g. e3) an Empty on its axis. Parent the planet arbors to it with matrix_parent_inverse set to identity and their location set to the axis offset in the carrier frame. Each child driver outputs its angle relative to the carrier, which is what the Willis solver produces. Pin-and-slot: with the output axis displaced by e in direction beta from the input axis, and the pin at radius r on the input, phi_out = phi_in + atan2(e*sin(phi_in-beta), r - e*cos(phi_in-beta)). This form is continuous because r > e, so no unwrapping is needed, and it is a valid simple expression. Verification must also check that the slot spans r +/- e and that its width equals the pin diameter plus clearance. For followers whose pin rides on an epicyclic gear, compute the pin position analytically and output phi = psi_mean + atan2(cross, dot) against a continuous mean angle psi_mean.
recommendations.api_details: Checked numerically against the unwrapped direct atan2: maximum difference 1.8e-15 rad. With e=1.1 mm and r=9.6 mm, the peak anomaly is asin(e/r)=6.58 deg and the pin travels 8.5 to 10.7 mm along the slot. The 1.1 mm eccentricity comes from Seiradakis (PoS); the 9.6 mm pin radius and 6.5 deg come from a secondary summary and should be confirmed in Freeth 2006 SI. Evaluated as a driver in 5.2.2, it gave 2.0991223 against 2.0991224 from the Python reference.

recommendations.topic: 2e. Spiral pointer followers and lookup-table drivers
recommendations.recommendation: Build each back-dial pointer (Metonic 5-turn, Saros 4-turn) as a rotating arm with a child 'follower' Empty or mesh that slides along the arm's local X. Drive the slide with rho(theta) from the spiral model in the spec. Anastasiou et al. 2014 reconstruct both spirals as half-circle spirals drawn from two centres; an Archimedean spiral is the common simplification. Keep both models as alternatives in the spec. Implement rho either in closed form, as a ternary on floor(theta/pi) using sqrt/cos/sin, within 255 characters, or as a lookup table stored in the driver's own F-curve: keyframes (x=theta, y=rho) with LINEAR interpolation evaluate any non-linear function of the driver value. The same lookup-table trick works for triangular-tooth contact kinematics.
recommendations.api_details: Since 5.0, drivers created in Python come with 2 default keyframes, (0,0) and (1,1), Bezier, with LINEAR extrapolation, instead of a Generator modifier. For a lookup table, call fc.keyframe_points.clear(), then kp.add(n), kp.foreach_set('co', float32 xy), then set interpolation='LINEAR', then fc.update(). Measured: 1,801 samples over 5 turns gave a maximum error of 6.0e-5 mm on the two-centre spiral.

recommendations.topic: 2f. Baked keyframes (secondary, for export only)
recommendations.recommendation: Treat drivers as the master. Bake only when exporting animation to glTF, USD or FBX, which do not carry drivers, or when freezing a render. Bake with bpy_extras.anim_utils.bake_action_objects, or write F-curves directly into the slotted action with foreach_set. Baked keys are float32 and cannot be cranked interactively. Do not use Python-function drivers from bpy.app.driver_namespace: a reopened .blend blocks them until the file is trusted (-y / --enable-autoexec or the Auto-Run preference), and the function must be registered again each session.
recommendations.api_details: Slotted-action API (4.4+; the legacy action.fcurves, groups and id_root were removed in 5.0): action.slots.new(id_type='OBJECT', name=...); layer=action.layers.new('L'); strip=layer.strips.new(type='KEYFRAME'); cb=strip.channelbag(slot, ensure=True); cb.fcurves.new(data_path, index=i). Alternatively use action.fcurve_ensure_for_datablock(obj, path, index=i) or bpy_extras.anim_utils.action_ensure_channelbag_for_slot(action, slot). Signature: bake_action_objects(object_action_pairs, *, frames, bake_options). FCurve functions: evaluate, bake, convert_to_samples.

recommendations.topic: 3a. Verification layer 1: exact 2D and analytic (outside Blender)
recommendations.recommendation: The main correctness proof runs outside Blender in pure numpy. Per meshing pair it checks a = m(z1+z2)/2 (or the profile-shifted value), contact ratio >= 1.2, tip clearance >= 0.25m, positive backlash, no undercut, and no tip interference below the other gear's base circle. It also samples one relative tooth pitch (the configuration is periodic in one pitch for identical involute teeth), about 50 samples, computing signed polygon distance or penetration between outlines near the line of centres. For non-meshing parts, use a swept-volume broad phase: each rotating body sweeps a solid of revolution (annulus [rmin, rmax] times [z0, z1]) about its axis; epicyclic bodies sweep about the carrier axis with widened radii. If two swept volumes are disjoint, the pair can never collide at any angle. Only the remaining pairs (meshes, pin/slot, pointer vs dial) need sampling. Add stack-up checks for axial layers and nested tubes: wall thickness and radial clearance. Freeth 2021 fits nine layers into 15.0 mm between b1 and the strap and 9.7 mm between the strap and the circular plate.
recommendations.api_details: Use explicit 2D cross products, x1*y2 - y1*x2: numpy 2.x deprecates np.cross on 2D vectors (a DeprecationWarning was observed with numpy 2.3.4).

recommendations.topic: 3b. Verification layer 2: inside Blender (BVHTree, readback, manifold)
recommendations.recommendation: (1) Driver readback: for N random crank values, set crank, call update_tag() and view_layer.update() (or frame_set), then compare every obj.matrix_world with the solver's float64 matrices; tolerance about 1e-4 rad because of float32. Also check the cycle identities, e.g. that pointers return to the same angle after M crank turns. (2) Interference: build world-space trees with BVHTree.FromPolygons(world_verts, tris, all_triangles=True) for each sample and require tree_a.overlap(tree_b) == []. FromObject returns object-local coordinates, so apply the transforms yourself in numpy. (3) Clearance: take the minimum of tree.find_nearest(Vector(p))[3] over flank vertices. (4) overlap() does not detect a part fully inside another; test containment with ray-cast parity or analytic radii. (5) Manifold check: bmesh with all(e.is_manifold for e in bm.edges) and bm.calc_volume(signed=True) > 0. Exit with a non-zero code on any failure.
recommendations.api_details: Signatures on 5.2.2: FromPolygons(vertices, polygons, *, all_triangles=False, epsilon=0.0); FromObject(object, depsgraph, *, deform=True, cage=False, epsilon=0.0); overlap(other_tree) -> list[(i, j)]; find_nearest(origin, distance) -> (co, normal, index, dist); ray_cast(origin, direction, distance). Source code: overlap uses an exact isect_tri_tri_v3, and epsilon only enlarges BVH bounds and affects shared-vertex filtering, so it does not act as a proximity threshold. Tests: coplanar or flush contacts return 0 or 4 depending on alignment, so they are unreliable; containment returns 0; epsilon=0.05 with a 0.01 gap returns 0. Cost measured: 4.3 ms per sample for a 64/38 pair (about 10k triangles each, rebuilding both trees). About 60 pairs times 50 samples comes to roughly 13 s.

recommendations.topic: 3c. Designing parts so checks are decidable
recommendations.recommendation: Give non-meshing layers explicit axial gaps of at least 0.1 to 0.2 mm in the spec, so that no two parts share coplanar faces unless the contact is intended. List intended contacts in the spec as a whitelist: gear seated on its arbor, pin in slot, follower in groove. Check these analytically instead of with BVH.
recommendations.api_details: Based on the degenerate-case BVH tests above.

recommendations.topic: 4. Rigid-body physics: not suitable for the gear train
recommendations.recommendation: Do not use Blender's Bullet rigid bodies to transmit motion through the teeth. The MESH collision shape is documented as 'rather slow and unstable'. Convex hulls erase the teeth. A compound of per-tooth convex children would need 223 children for b1. The collision margin (default 0.04 in scene units) is as large as the 0.05 mm backlash at mm scale. Contact solving drifts and slips, so exact rational ratios over 19- to 76-year cycles cannot be reproduced. Blender exposes no gear-coupling constraint. For this project, 'physically functional' means: involute conjugate teeth with correct centre distances, positive backlash, contact ratio >= 1.2, no interference at any sampled or swept configuration, exact kinematics proven with rational arithmetic and confirmed by driver readback, and manifold, toleranced, printable parts. At most, keep a separate two-gear rigid-body demo scene as an illustration.
recommendations.api_details: On 5.2.2, RigidBodyConstraint.type offers FIXED, POINT, HINGE, SLIDER, PISTON, GENERIC, GENERIC_SPRING, MOTOR, with no gear type. collision_shape offers BOX, SPHERE, CAPSULE, CYLINDER, CONE, CONVEX_HULL, MESH, COMPOUND. RigidBodyWorld has substeps_per_frame, solver_iterations and use_split_impulse.

recommendations.topic: 5a. Materials: bronze PBR, patina and evidence colour-coding
recommendations.recommendation: Use a single Principled BSDF for bronze: Metallic 1, Roughness 0.25 to 0.45, and Specular Tint for the F82 edge tint (4.0+). Physicallybased.info has no bronze entry. Its copper is linear (0.932, 0.623, 0.522) and its brass is (0.910, 0.778, 0.423); interpolate towards about (0.92, 0.70, 0.47) and label this as an approximation. Patina layer: Metallic 0, Roughness about 0.8, verdigris greens and dark cuprite browns. Mix the two using Ambient Occlusion (works in Cycles and EEVEE), Geometry Pointiness (Cycles only, needs dense meshes) and Noise Texture through a Color Ramp. Drive the mix factor from a controller property 'patina' so one switch goes from 'museum fragment' to 'as new'. Add a debug view that colours objects by status (SURVIVING, RECONSTRUCTED, HYPOTHETICAL) through obj.color with Solid/Workbench shading set to OBJECT colour.
recommendations.api_details: Principled BSDF inputs on 5.2.2 include 'Base Color', 'Metallic', 'Roughness', 'IOR', 'Specular IOR Level', 'Specular Tint', 'Anisotropic', 'Coat Weight', 'Coat Roughness', 'Thin Film Thickness'. Node idnames: ShaderNodeBsdfPrincipled, ShaderNodeAmbientOcclusion, ShaderNodeNewGeometry, ShaderNodeTexNoise, ShaderNodeValToRGB, ShaderNodeMix, ShaderNodeBevel. bpy.data.materials.new() already comes with a node tree (Principled plus Output); Material.use_nodes raises a DeprecationWarning (removal planned for 6.0).

recommendations.topic: 5b. Rendering: Cycles on Apple Silicon Metal, EEVEE previews and command lines
recommendations.recommendation: Final renders: Cycles with the METAL device. MetalRT set to AUTO uses hardware ray tracing on M3 and later, including the M4. Use OIDN denoising on the GPU and persistent data for animations. Previews: EEVEE, engine id 'BLENDER_EEVEE' again since 5.0. The first Cycles Metal render compiles kernels: 124 s measured on this M4, then 0.41 s in the next process thanks to the cache. Run one warm-up render before any benchmark. A headless EEVEE render worked in 3.9 s.
recommendations.api_details: cp=bpy.context.preferences.addons['cycles'].preferences; cp.compute_device_type='METAL'; cp.get_devices(); for d in cp.devices: d.use=(d.type=='METAL'). The M4 is listed as 'Apple M4 (GPU - 8 cores)'. Then cp.metalrt='AUTO' (OFF/ON/AUTO), scene.render.engine='CYCLES', scene.cycles.device='GPU', scene.cycles.denoiser='OPENIMAGEDENOISE', scene.cycles.denoising_use_gpu=True (factory default is False), scene.render.use_persistent_data=True. Since 5.0, set image_settings.media_type ('IMAGE'|'MULTI_LAYER_IMAGE'|'VIDEO') before file_format. The ffmpeg codecs include H264, H265, PRORES and AV1. CLI: blender -b out/am.blend -E CYCLES -o //renders/am_#### -s 1 -e 480 -a -- --cycles-device METAL. Arguments run in order, so put the file first and -a last.

recommendations.topic: 5c. Export for 3D printing (STL, 3MF) with tolerances
recommendations.recommendation: Keep a 'print profile' in the spec, separate from the scholarly geometry: a scale factor, circumferential backlash implemented by thinning teeth (0.1 to 0.2 mm total at print scale), extra centre distance (about +0.2 mm at module 1, +0.15 to 0.2 at module 2), bore clearance and axial gaps of 0.2 to 0.3 mm. Regenerate the print geometry from the same code with these offsets and run the same verification again. At 1:1 the module is about 0.5, which FDM cannot print well (the sweet spot is module 1.5 to 2 with a 0.4 mm nozzle). Use resin, or scale by 2 or more: b1 at module 1 is about 223 mm in pitch diameter. Export STL with the native operator, one file per part. For 3MF, which carries units, write a small stdlib exporter (zipfile plus XML) that you can unit-test, or install the maintained extension. Check meshes with the 3D Print Toolbox extension.
recommendations.api_details: bpy.ops.wm.stl_export(filepath=..., export_selected_objects=True, use_batch=True, global_scale=1.0, use_scene_unit=False, apply_modifiers=True, evaluation_mode='DAG_EVAL_RENDER', ascii_format=False, forward_axis='Y', up_axis='Z'). Parameters verified on 5.2.2; evaluation_mode is new in 5.2. The legacy bpy.ops.export_mesh.stl is gone (bpy.ops.export_mesh is empty). Keep use_scene_unit=False so that 1 BU is written as 1 mm, and confirm with a re-import test. Minimal 3MF (Core Spec v1.4.0): [Content_Types].xml, _rels/.rels, 3D/3dmodel.model with <model unit='millimeter'>, <vertices>/<triangles>, <build><item>, manifold, outward normals. Extension option: 3MF Import/Export by Clonephaze, v2.7.7, Blender 4.2+, primary target 5.0, Python API io_mesh_3mf.api.export_3mf; its operator id and the bl_ext module path still need checking after install (blender -c extension install -s -e <pkg>). 3D Print Toolbox is v1.4.1 for 4.2+.

recommendations.topic: 6a. Project and file structure
recommendations.recommendation: Suggested layout: antikythera/ with spec/ (gears.toml, arbors.toml, joints.toml, dials.toml, cycles.toml [targets with sources], print_profiles.toml, schema.json); am/ as the pure package (spec.py, kinematics.py [Fraction solver, Willis, pin-slot], expr.py [emits and lints simple expressions and evaluates them in Python], involute.py, triangular.py, outline.py [loops with holes, spokes, square bores], interference2d.py, swept.py, astro_checks.py, svg_plan.py [2D plan drawings straight from the outlines, the 'plan' deliverable], threemf.py, verify.py [CLI, JSON report, non-zero exit on failure]); blender_scripts/ (bootstrap.py [sys.path and argv parsing], build.py [idempotent: wipes the AM_* collections and stores the spec sha256 in scene['am_spec_sha256']], animate.py [controller, drivers, followers], materials.py, check.py [readback, BVH, manifold], export_print.py, render.py); tests/ (unittest); out/ (generated, never edited by hand).
recommendations.api_details: Each Blender script starts with: sys.path.insert(0, repo_root) (the explicit insert is the safe choice); argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--')+1:] if '--' in sys.argv else []; and importlib.reload(...) when iterating in the GUI.

recommendations.topic: 6b. Running on macOS (headless and interactive)
recommendations.recommendation: Add alias blender=/Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender to ~/.zshrc. The manual instead suggests adding that directory to /etc/paths, which needs sudo. Pipeline: PY=/Applications/Blender.app/Contents/Resources/5.2/python/bin/python3.13; $PY -m unittest discover -s tests -v; $PY -m am.verify spec/; blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P blender_scripts/build.py -- --spec spec --out out/am.blend; blender -b out/am.blend --python-exit-code 1 -P blender_scripts/check.py -- --samples 50; blender -b out/am.blend --python-exit-code 1 -P blender_scripts/export_print.py -- --profile fdm_x2; blender -b out/am.blend -P blender_scripts/render.py -- --preset final; open -a Blender out/am.blend for interactive use. Because the drivers are simple expressions, the saved .blend animates without Auto-Run. --factory-startup gives reproducible runs but does not load user extensions: enable any needed extension explicitly, or better, use the stdlib 3MF writer.
recommendations.api_details: Useful flags on 5.2.2: -b, -P/--python, --python-expr, --python-exit-code N, -y/--enable-autoexec, -Y, --factory-startup, -E, -o, -s, -e, -a, -f, -t, --cycles-device METAL (after --), --addons, --offline-mode, and -c extension {install,list,sync,...}. In -b mode the gpu module needs gpu.init() (5.2) before any Python GPU drawing; rendering itself does not.

recommendations.topic: 6c. Unit-testing outside Blender
recommendations.recommendation: Test the pure package with the bundled python3.13 and unittest, which need no install. Cover: exact ratio and cycle identities (Fraction); expression linting (length <= 255, only allowed names) and Python evaluation of the same strings; involute invariants (base pitch = pi*m*cos(alpha); tooth thickness at the pitch circle; outline closed and non-self-intersecting); the pin-slot identity against an unwrapped direct atan2; the spiral-follower function; the 2D interference detector on known-good and half-pitch-shifted pairs; swept-volume logic; and the 3MF writer (re-read the zip and check manifoldness). Code that needs bpy or mathutils is tested by 'blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P tests_blender/run.py'. Optional later step, not done in planning: create a venv from the bundled interpreter with --system-site-packages and pip install pytest, shapely for polygon cross-checks, and, if you want to import bpy under pytest, the official bpy==5.2.2 wheel (cp313, macOS arm64, 245 MB).
recommendations.api_details: On PyPI, bpy 5.2.2 was released 2026-09-15 with Requires-Python ==3.13.*; the wheel is bpy-5.2.2-cp313-cp313-macosx_11_0_arm64.whl.
